extracted.intended_audience: Filipino citizens (for the Decalogue) and users/distributors of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: A historic political/moral decalogue addressed to Filipino citizens (Mabini's Ten Commandments) accompanied by the Project Gutenberg full license and distribution requirements for the eBook. The page contains prescriptive moral rules and legal/procedural rules for copying and distributing the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: First — Love God and thy honor above all things
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt love God and thy honor above all things: God as the fountain of all truth, of all justice and of all activity; and thy honor, the only power which will oblige thee to be faithful, just and industrious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a primary moral obligation: prioritize divine truth and personal honor as the foundation of faithfulness, justice, and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second — Worship God according to conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt worship God in the form which thy conscience may deem most righteous and worthy: for in thy conscience, which condemns thy evil deeds and praises thy good ones, speaks thy God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms freedom of conscience in religious practice; conscience is the voice of God in moral evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third — Cultivate your special gifts; pursue perfection and contribute to humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt cultivate the special gifts which God has granted thee, working and studying according to thy ability, never leaving the path of righteousness and justice, in order to attain thy own perfection, by means whereof thou shalt contribute to the progress of humanity...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for personal development through work and study within ethical bounds so one may serve humanity and glorify God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth — Love thy country after God and thy honor, more than thyself
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt love thy country after God and thy honor and more than thyself: for she is the only Paradise which God has given thee in this life, the only patrimony of thy race, the only inheritance of thy ancestors and the only hope of thy posterity...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places patriotic duty high among obligations, framing the country as the collective inheritance and hope for future generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifth — Strive for the happiness of thy country before thy own
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt strive for the happiness of thy country before thy own, making of her the kingdom of reason, of justice and of labor: for if she be happy, thou, together with thy family, shalt likewise be happy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates prioritizing national welfare and building a society of reason, justice, and productive labor as the path to individual well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixth — Strive for the independence of thy country
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt strive for the independence of thy country: for only thou canst have any real interest in her advancement and exaltation, because her independence constitutes thy own liberty; her advancement, thy perfection; and her exaltation, thy own glory and immortality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links national independence directly to individual liberty, perfection, and legacy; encourages active pursuit of sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventh — Recognize only authority elected by the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt not recognize in thy country the authority of any person who has not been elected by thee and thy countrymen; for authority emanates from God, and as God speaks in the conscience of every man, the person designated and proclaimed by the conscience of a whole people is the only one who can use true authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts popular sovereignty and rejects illegitimate (unelected) authority; grounds legitimacy in the people's conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighth — Strive for a Republic and never for a monarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt strive for a Republic and never for a monarchy in thy country: for the latter exalts one or several families and founds a dynasty; the former makes a people noble and worthy through reason, great through liberty, and prosperous and brilliant through labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative endorsement of republican government over monarchy, tying republicanism to equality, liberty, and prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ninth — Love thy neighbor as thyself, but defend self-preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself: ... but if thy neighbor, failing in this sacred duty, attempt against thy life, thy liberty and thy interests, then thou shalt destroy and annihilate him for the supreme law of self-preservation prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands mutual aid and restraint but permits defensive action, including extreme measures, if a neighbor attacks one's life, liberty, or interests (self-preservation principle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenth — Consider thy countryman more than thy neighbor; perfect national solidarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou shalt consider thy countryman more than thy neighbor; thou shalt see him thy friend, thy brother or at least thy comrade, with whom thou art bound by one fate, by the same joys and sorrows and by common aspirations and interests.... unite in a perfect solidarity of purpose and interest...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands preferential solidarity with fellow countrymen to build collective strength against common enemies and pursue shared aims.
